newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to mass-produce hybrids in 1997-report.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to mass-produce hybrids in 1997-report.

text.p: Japan's Toyota Motors announced it is to mass-produce the world's first production-line hybrid petrol- and electric-powered car within a year, the daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper reported on Sunday.
Toyota plans to turn out tens of thousands of the new hybrid by the end of 1997, aiming at a price tag of around 2.5 million yen ($22,500), said the daily.

The Japanese car maker has beaten its close competitors in the hybrid market -- France's Renault, America's Ford Motors and Mitsubishi Motors -- to the launch of a new breed of environmentally friendly vehicles, the newspaper said.

The hybrid will boast a two-fold increase in petrol economy compared to Toyota's current "Corolla" model, according to company sources, said the Nihon Keizai Shimbun. The car maker said the hybrid can re-route dead power, generated by the petrol engine but not used for locomotion, to the car's battery, to be used later by the electric motor.

The petrol-saving strategy has economic attractions. The hybrid will have a range of 70 miles to 84 miles (113-135 km) to the gallon - and should appeal to environmentally conscious consumers because of a reduced contribution to the greenhouse effect, claimed the Japanese car maker.

Toyota said it will keep the cost of the hybrid down - already several thousand dollars more expensive than a petrol engine of similar size - in order to create a new market consciousness for hybrid vehicles, the daily said.
The Japanese car maker said it is targeting the American market first because of an growing shift in the United States towards low-pollution cars, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
